c.tagline: UNESCO gastronomy capital of baklava, pistachios, and Roman mosaics.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered; Uber connects you to licensed metered taxis rather than private cars. Confirm the meter is running at the start of the ride.

emergency.note: 112 is Türkiye's unified emergency number, connecting to police, ambulance, and fire services.

avoid.reason: Avoid districts along the Syrian border outside the city; central Gaziantep itself is fine.
Usual pickpocket awareness in the crowded Bakırcılar coppersmith bazaar.

hood_desc: The restored historic core (Old City) of stone mansions, hans, and narrow lanes around Gaziantep Castle and the Zeugma Mosaic Museum; best for first-timers who want boutique hotels in Ottoman-era buildings within walking distance of the main sights.

The busy commercial and administrative heart of the Şahinbey district, lined with shops, restaurants, and mid-range hotels along Atatürk Boulevard; a convenient, well-connected base in the middle of the city.

Gaziantep's modern, greener northern district of wide avenues, malls, and international-brand hotels around Mücahitler and İbrahimli; suits business travelers and those wanting newer, quieter accommodation.

The atmospheric Coppersmiths' Bazaar (Bakırcılar Çarşısı) quarter and adjoining covered markets, where artisans still hammer copper and sell spices, baklava, and antiques; ideal for shoppers and food lovers.

The Castle quarter (Kaleiçi) at the foot of Gaziantep Castle, dense with traditional courtyard houses, kebab houses, and the copper and spice bazaars; a characterful, sights-heavy base close to the old town.

transit.hours: Trams and buses generally run from around 6:00 AM to midnight; Gaziray commuter trains run through the day at regular intervals.
transit.note: Gaziulaş runs the city's public transport: roughly 70 bus routes, three tram lines, and the Gaziray commuter rail crossing the city east–west. The T1 tram is the most useful line for visitors, linking the railway station area through the central districts.
transit.pay: Fares are paid with the rechargeable Gazikart smart card, tapped on board buses and trams and at Gaziray stations. Cards are sold at kiosks and station machines.

bus: Intercity coaches from Gaziantep Otogar to Şanlıurfa, Adana, and beyond
train: Gaziantep railway station (TCDD regional and sleeper services to Adana, Malatya, and connections onward)

transit.m: Municipal bus to city center (~45-60 min)

tip.r: Rounding up the bill or leaving about 5-10% for good service in restaurants is appreciated but not obligatory.
